accounting_contract.why: pi usage.input excludes the cache buckets on both legs (E17 §3, E17B §2); treating it as provider raw input_tokens under-counts gross by ~5.5x

at_20pct.reading: 'passes beyond parity' means the 95% interval lies wholly below 1.0, i.e. the resident arm buys fewer gross tokens than retrieval, not merely as many

i_gross_ordering_across_budgets.question: where the gross ratio sits relative to 1.0 across the budget sweep, and whether at c = 20% it passes beyond parity

ii_cost_ratio_at_2_5_percent.question: whether the cost ratio stays below 1.0 at c = 2.5%

iii_window_fixed_vs_E27.caveat: the two cells also differ in schedule seed (4352 vs 4200) and sessions built (24 vs 12), so this is read, not causally attributed to the window
iii_window_fixed_vs_E27.question: the difference between E27 (steady state, S13-S24, c = 10%) and E28-O-10 with the window held fixed

budget.note: pi_reported is what was actually charged at pi's catalog rates; standard is the judged rate card, which is >= catalog on both providers

resident_utilization_trajectory.note: a growth window: the resident set is not expected to fill. The trajectory is an INPUT state quantity, fixed by the schedule and the model-free policy replay before any model call.

bootstrap.method: paired percentile bootstrap over sessions, common random numbers
